injuryReport.name: Amik Robertson
injuryReport.beatComment: Robertson was unable to play against the Bengals on Monday due to an ankle injury that he picked up during Friday's practice. He would need to log a limited session over the next two days to have a chance at playing against the Cardinals on Sunday.

injuryReport.name: Stefon Diggs
factors: Wednesday rest/non-participation alongside active medical tag (Personal); awaiting Thursday participation
injuryReport.beatComment: Diggs was away from the team for Wednesday's session due to a personal issue. There's no indication this will be a long-term absence, and the Commanders did excuse him for Wednesday. Still, Diggs' return to the team will be worth monitoring over the coming days in advance of Sunday's game at Arizona.

injuryReport.name: Treylon Burks
factors: Wednesday Limited Participation (LP); player toughness prior = 76%
injuryReport.beatComment: Burks presumably had his reps capped for maintenance purposes, as the wideout was sidelined for the Commanders' Week 9 loss to the Rams due to the same foot issue before suiting up in the ensuing two contests. In both of those games, Burks played north of 60 percent of the offensive snaps while producing a combined 4-57-0 receiving line on six targets. Provided he advances to full practice activity by Friday, Burks should head into this weekend's game in Arizona without a designation.

injuryReport.name: Charles Omenihu
factors: Wednesday Limited Participation (LP); player toughness prior = 78%

injuryReport.name: John Bates
injuryReport.beatComment: Bates went without a target for the fourth straight game. The 29-year-old's 21 offensive snaps ranked third at tight end behind Chig Okonkwo (49) and Ben Sinnott (24), and Bates should continue to have no fantasy value in Week 12 versus the Cardinals.

injuryReport.name: Rachaad White
injuryReport.beatComment: With Jacory Croskey-Merritt back from a four-game absence due to a groin injury, White saw a season-low 15 snaps on offense, and the latter's lone carry early in the fourth quarter was nullified by a defensive offside penalty. Croskey-Merritt and Austin Ekeler were responsible for 20 of the Commanders' 26 rushing attempts Monday, and it looks like the return of the former has squeezed White out of the offensive gameplan. The Commanders will hit the road for each of their next two games, starting with Sunday against the Cardinals.

injuryReport.name: Jayden Daniels
injuryReport.beatComment: Daniels looked like he was on his way to a middling night during a first half in which he led the Commanders to just seven points, but the 2024 first-round pick flipped a switch in the second half, particularly in the fourth quarter. Daniels led field-goal drives of 13, 11 and five plays that netted a total of 193 yards during the final period, the last one featuring strikes of 22 and 42 yards to Antonio Williams to position Drew Stevens for a game-winning field goal. Daniels finished with his second-highest passing yardage total of the season, and he also mustered his seventh interception-free effort of the campaign. Having helped Washington to a critical victory, he'll look to carry the momentum over into a favorable Week 12 road matchup against the Cardinals on Sunday.

injuryReport.name: Quan Martin
injuryReport.beatComment: Martin's practice reps were limited both Thursday and Friday due to a shoulder issue, but his full session Saturday was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Monday night's game. Martin could see an uptick in defensive snaps if defensive back Amik Robertson (ankle) is not cleared to play against Cincinnati.

injuryReport.name: Colson Yankoff
injuryReport.beatComment: Yankoff sat out the Commanders' contest against the Giants in Week 10 because of a knee injury, but it now looks like he's put it behind him. He figures to resume a depth role at tight end in Week 11 against the Bengals.

irReserve.name: Laremy Tunsil
factors: On Injured Reserve — 21-day practice window not yet opened
irReserve.beatComment: Tunsil underwent surgery in August to repair a torn triceps. The left tackle continues to recover, but he likely will not suit up for the Commanders in 2026 unless the team makes a playoff run. Even then, it remains unclear whether Tunsil would be able to return at all before the 2027 season.

coachingMatchup.headline: Mike LaFleur & DC Nick Rallis vs. HC Dan Quinn, OC David Blough & DC Daronte Jones (State Farm Stadium)
coachingMatchup.summary: Week 12 two-sided coordinator chess match pitting Arizona Cardinals's staff (Mike LaFleur, OC Nathaniel Hackett, DC Nick Rallis) against Washington Commanders (4-5-1)—testing both Arizona's offensive efficiency and its defensive pass-rush and coverage discipline.
bullets: Pass-Game Efficiency & Coverage Shell Delta: Mike LaFleur and OC Nathaniel Hackett pair condensed splits with pre-snap jet motion and orbit motion to stress Washington Commanders's single-high vs. two-high rotations—widening curl/flat defenders to attack the honey-hole between hook/curl linebackers and deep safeties on play-action choice/dagger concepts.

Trench Run-Fit & Two-Way Leverage: Against Washington Commanders's pin-and-pull, counter, and duo runs targeting the A- and B-gaps, DC Nick Rallis balances four-man pressure with disguised Quarters and Cover 6 split-safety rotations on early downs and in the red zone.

Money-Down & Red-Zone Execution: Third-down conversion discipline and red-zone touchdown rate govern whether Arizona sustains multi-play scoring drives or yields momentum to Washington Commanders's pass rush and coverage disguises.
Tempo, Turnovers & Venue Leverage: State Farm Stadium situational play-calling, penalty margin, and turnover differential provide the clearest late-game swing factors for both coaching staffs.

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Josh Johnson, Trey McBride & Simi Fehoko vs. CB Rasul Douglas & LB Odafe Oweh
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: ARI: #23 Pass Off (196.1 yds) · #25 Off. Scoring (-3.29) | WAS: #20 Pass Def (+2.63)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Josh Johnson, Trey McBride & Simi Fehoko attack the intermediate seams and middle-of-the-field leverage windows against Washington Commanders's #20 pass defense (+2.63). Winning early-down timing throws keeps Arizona's offense ahead of the chains and punishes disguised single-high rotations.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Watch Josh Johnson (#9) scanning Commanders's deep safeties at the snap—when LB Odafe Oweh widens to take away the crossers, the intermediate seam opens immediately for Trey McBride (#85).

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Walter Nolen III, Dante Stills & Roy Lopez vs. QB Jayden Daniels & G Brandon Coleman
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: ARI: #16 Def Sacks (2.3/gm) | WAS: #16 Pass Protection (6.5%)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Walter Nolen III, Dante Stills & Roy Lopez lead Arizona's #16 NFL pass rush (2.3/gm) against Washington Commanders's #16 pass-protection unit (6.5%). Collapsing the interior pocket without sending extra blitzers lets Cardinals keep seven defenders in coverage.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: On 3rd-and-6+, watch whether Walter Nolen III (#97) draw chip help from Commanders's tight ends or backs—creating 1-on-1 rush lanes inside for Dante Stills (#55).

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Mack Wilson Sr., Budda Baker & Denzel Burke vs. WR Antonio Williams & QB Jayden Daniels
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: ARI: #31 Pass Def (+7.78) | WAS: #19 Pass Off (217.0 yds)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Mack Wilson Sr., Budda Baker & Denzel Burke anchor Arizona's #31 pass defense (+7.78) against WR Antonio Williams and Washington Commanders's #19 passing attack (217.0 yds). Limiting explosive 20+ yard chunk plays forces Commanders into sustained red-zone drives.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Track Mack Wilson Sr. (#1) at the top of routes against WR Antonio Williams: press-bail alignment with safety help over the top takes away QB Jayden Daniels's preferred isolation shots.

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Tyler Allgeier & Harrison Wallace III vs. Commanders Front Seven & LB Odafe Oweh
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: ARI: #27 Rush Off (93.9 yds) | WAS: #28 Rush Def (+0.51)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Tyler Allgeier & Harrison Wallace III test Washington Commanders's #28 run defense (+0.51) with horizontal stretch and interior cutback lanes. Generating 4.5+ yards on first down unlocks play-action explosives and neutralizes Commanders's pass-rush packages.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Watch whether Commanders's linebackers over-pursue motion to the perimeter—opening decisive backside B-gap cutback lanes for Tyler Allgeier (#22).

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Isaac Seumalo, Elijah Wilkinson & Isaiah Adams vs. DT Tim Settle & Commanders Simulated Pressures
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: ARI: #16 Pass Protection (6.0%) | WAS: #16 Def Sacks (2.4/gm)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Isaac Seumalo, Elijah Wilkinson & Isaiah Adams protect Josh Johnson (#16 protection at 6.0%) against DT Tim Settle and Washington Commanders's #16 pass rush (2.4/gm). Passing off interior twists and simulated blitzes cleanly determines late-down conversion efficiency.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Watch Isaac Seumalo (#73) on obvious passing downs—if DT Tim Settle cannot win clean around the arc, Commanders must dial up interior stunts that stress Elijah Wilkinson (#65).
